props.gloss_en: the mishna: one who tears in his anger is exempt
the mishna: one who tears over his dead is exempt
the baraita: one who tears in his mourning or over his dead is liable
the baraita: one who tears in his anger is liable
and though he desecrates Shabbat, he has fulfilled [the duty of] tearing
this [the baraita: liable] is of his own dead
that [the mishna: exempt] is of any [unrelated] dead
actually [the mishna is] of his own dead, and of those [relatives] who are not subject to mourning
the baraita as cited: a Sage who died -- all are his relatives
rather say: all are LIKE his relatives -- all tear for him, all bare [the shoulder] for him, all eat the mourners' meal for him in the square
the baraita as cited: why do a man's sons and daughters die when young? so that he weep and mourn for an upright man
rather: because he did not weep and mourn for an upright man
for whoever weeps for an upright man is forgiven all his sins, on account of the honour he did
R' Shimon b. Elazar: one standing by the dead at the time the soul departs is obliged to tear
to what is this like? to a Torah scroll that was burnt
this [the baraita: liable for tearing in anger] is R' Yehuda
that [the mishna: exempt] is R' Shimon
R' Yehuda, who said: [for] a labour not needed for its own sake one is liable
R' Shimon, who said: [for] a labour not needed for its own sake one is exempt
R' Avin: this one too is repairing
for he gives satisfaction to his inclination
R' Yochanan b. Nuri: one who tears his garments in his anger -- let him be in your eyes as one who worships idols
...and one who breaks his vessels in his anger
...and one who scatters his money in his anger
for such is the craft of the evil inclination: today it says to him do this, tomorrow do that, until it says to him worship idols, and he goes and worships
R' Avin: what is the verse? 'there shall be no strange god in you, nor shall you bow to a foreign god' (Ps 81:10) -- which strange god is within a man's body? say: the evil inclination
it is needed only where he does it to cast fear on his household
Rav Yehuda pulled out the fringes [of a garment]
Rav Acha bar Yaakov broke broken vessels
Rav Sheshet threw muninei on his maidservant's head
R' Abba broke a lid
Bar Kappara: whoever sheds tears over an upright man -- the Holy One counts them and lays them up in His treasury
as it is said: 'You have counted my wanderings; put my tears in Your flask; are they not in Your book?' (Ps 56:9)
Rav: whoever is lazy in eulogising a Sage deserves to be buried alive
as it is said: 'they buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnat Serach... north of Mount Gaash' (Josh 24:30) -- teaching that the mountain raged against them to kill them
R' Yochanan: whoever is lazy in eulogising a Sage does not live long -- measure for measure
as it is said: 'in full measure (besase'a), when You send her away, You contend with her' (Is 27:8)
'and the people served the Lord all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who lengthened days after Joshua' (Judg 2:7)
R' Yochanan: Babylonian! they lengthened days; years they did not lengthen
but then: 'that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied' (Deut 11:21) -- days and not years?
R' Yochanan: one of the brothers who died -- all the brothers should worry; one of a fellowship who died -- the whole fellowship should worry
some say: [it is] where the eldest died
and some say: where the youngest died
